The gold in a ring was probably forged when two dead stars collided.
In July 2025, satellites caught one. Gamma rays, gone in half a second.
Then the sky refused to go dark. X-rays poured out for almost ten minutes, a record for a merger.
Astronomers traced it to a galaxy whose light left six billion years ago, and ruled out a supernova.
The best fit: two neutron stars, each crushed to the width of a city, merging into a spinning magnet, a magnetar.
Its magnetic field may have kept feeding the blast. That's still a hypothesis, from one event.
And crashes like this are thought to forge gold. Your ring may be their leftovers.
